newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney Olympics sign US$135 mln Japanese TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Sydney Olympics sign US$135 mln Japanese TV deal.

text.p: Sydney 2000 Olympics organisers on Friday announced a US$135 million Japanese television rights deal with a consortium headed by Japan's NHK.
The Sydney Olympics organisers also announced an US$11 million television broadcast rights deal for South America.
They said they had now raised US$1.66 billion in television broadcast rights, compared with their budgeted US$948 million.

Australia's Olympics Minister Michael Knight said the Japanese deal was a record. The Atlanta Olympics this year received US$99.5 million from Japanese broadcasters, with Sydney originally budgeting to receive US$100 million.

"This is an endorsement for the Sydney Olympics," Knight said at a press conference in Sydney, adding that Sydney Olympic organisers SOCOG would receive some 60 percent of the major television contracts.
"This is an enormous vote of confidence for the Sydney Olympics and a reflection of a very high expectation of the television rights and sponsorship," Knight said.

The Sydney Olympics have already sold the United States television broadcast rights to the NBC network for US$715 million, European Broadcasting Union rights for US$350 million and the Australian rights to Channel Seven for US$45 million.
"The Japanese rights came in over SOCOG's budgeted figure of US$100 million and the agreement continues Sydney's outstanding success in the sales of overseas television rights for 2000," said Knight.
"SOCOG alreay has more money in television rights than the entire TV budget, but we still have a number of countries that have still not completed talks," Knight said.
Knight said television rights had still to be negotiated with Canada, New Zealand, South Africa and parts of Asia, such as South Korea, worth about US$60 million.
